defects.description: The prefix tie-break in `_prerelease_lt` compares lengths with `>` instead of `<`, so when one prerelease tuple is a prefix of the other the longer identifier list is ranked as lower precedence, inverting the order of e.g. `1.0.0-alpha` and `1.0.0-alpha.1`.
paraphrases: After all shared prerelease identifiers compare equal, SemVer says the version with more fields wins, but the length comparison is reversed so the shorter one is treated as greater.
`1.0.0-alpha` should sort before `1.0.0-alpha.1`; the flipped length test makes the one with extra identifiers sort first instead.
The final same-prefix ordering decision returns the wrong boolean because it asks whether the left tuple is longer rather than shorter.
defects.rationale: Correct form: 'return len(left) < len(right)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The non-zero-major caret upper bound in `_caret_bounds` keeps the original `minor` instead of zeroing it, so `^1.2.0` compiles to `< 2.<minor>.0` and wrongly admits next-major releases such as `2.0.0`.
paraphrases: When bumping the major for a caret bound, the minor component is carried over rather than reset to 0, pushing the exclusive ceiling past the intended `2.0.0` line.
`^1.2.x` is supposed to stop below the next major (`<2.0.0`), but the ceiling is built with the old minor, letting `2.0.0` satisfy the range.
The upper comparator for a caret range fails to zero out the minor field after incrementing major, so versions in the next major series leak in.
defects.rationale: Correct form: 'high = Version(major + 1, 0, 0)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The `=` case in `_Comparator.allows` returns `candidate != target`, inverting exact-match so an exact-version range matches every version except the one it names.
paraphrases: Equality was replaced with inequality in the exact-match comparator, so `satisfies('1.2.3', '1.2.3')` returns False while unrelated versions pass.
The `=` operator now accepts anything that differs from its target and rejects the target itself, exactly backwards.
An exact pin is treated as an exclusion filter because the comparison for the `=` operator is negated.
defects.rationale: Correct form: 'return candidate == target'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: `max_satisfying` keeps a candidate when it is `<` the current best instead of `>`, so it returns the lowest satisfying version rather than the highest.
defects.anchor: best is None or candidate < best
paraphrases: The running-best update in `max_satisfying` prefers smaller versions, making the function behave like a min instead of the documented max.
Because the retained candidate must be less than the incumbent, the selection walks down to the minimum satisfying version.
The comparison that should track the largest matching version is reversed, yielding the smallest match.
defects.rationale: Correct form: 'best is None or candidate > best'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.
